q: What are the four parts that make an agent different from a chatbot?
options: Speed, price, colour and internet access
Standing instructions, memory, tools, and a trigger
A subscription, an app, a laptop and a password
explanation: An agent has (1) standing instructions: its role and rules; (2) memory: your context and templates; (3) tools: what it may use; and (4) a trigger: when it works. A chatbot answers and stops.

q: What is a 'harness', in plain words?
options: The paid subscription that gives you agents
The scaffolding around the AI that holds its instructions, memory and routine together
The physical cable connecting your phone to the internet
explanation: The harness is the scaffolding that holds the instructions, memory and routine together. Your Playbook is the start of one, and you have been building it all week.

q: Which is the main method taught for installing your persona on any phone, for free?
options: Paste-the-persona: paste your persona block at the start of each new work chat
Write the persona into your email signature
Wait for the platform to do it automatically
explanation: The paste-the-persona method costs nothing and works on any phone, so it is the main method. Platform features such as custom instructions or Saved Info are optional extras, if your free tier has them.

q: How does the lesson show you an agent working, using only a phone and free tools?
options: By watching the instructor's screen recording of a paid agent
By sending one request with and without the persona block, then comparing the answers
By buying a subscription before Day 9 starts
You cannot see an agent working without paying for one
explanation: Instead of a recording, you run a five-minute comparison yourself: the briefed chat against the unbriefed one. What you build is the free-tools version: the same four parts, on your own phone.
